transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical support. My name is Sean. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Sean. I'm calling because I've spent all morning trying to set up remote access for our new home CCTV security cameras, but the port forwarding rules on the S-Net Hub keep failing and I cannot connect from outside our home network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you configure port forwarding and dynamic DNS on your hub, Connor. Before we access your router's firewall rules, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 58 St. Albans Road, Watford, WD17 1TN. And my security question answer is my first car model, Ford Fiesta.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Connor, that verifies your account file. What specific ports does your CCTV system require?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The camera system uses port 8000 for video streams and port 554 for RTSP streaming. Sean, our house was broken into three nights ago while my wife and two young children were asleep upstairs! The intruders smashed through the patio doors, and my wife has been so traumatized that she cannot sleep and is terrified to stay in the house alone unless she can check the CCTV cameras on her phone! We desperately need this working today!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us check whether your broadband connection is assigned a public IPv4 address or sitting behind carrier-grade NAT.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay... please, whatever we need to get these cameras viewable on our phones.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am opening your WAN connection profile on our radius server to inspect your gateway lease.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the gateway lease tell us?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your optical line is currently provisioned on a dynamic public IPv4 address starting with 82.14, which confirms carrier-grade NAT is not active.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That means port forwarding will work without carrier blocks?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, having a dedicated dynamic public IP allows incoming traffic on specific ports to traverse the router firewall directly to your NVR recorder.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we open the ports inside the router?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open your web browser, navigate to 192.168.1.254, and log in with your administrator password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Navigating to 192.168.1.254... typing the admin password... logged into the S-Net Hub manager.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on Advanced Settings, then select Firewall, and click on Port Forwarding.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Advanced Settings... Firewall... Port Forwarding. I see a table for adding new port forwarding rules.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, we must assign a static DHCP reservation for your CCTV Network Video Recorder so its local IP address never changes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where do I set the static IP reservation?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on DHCP Table, locate the MAC address of the Hikvision NVR, and assign it permanent IP 192.168.1.150.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found the Hikvision NVR... reserved IP address 192.168.1.150. Saved.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now return to Port Forwarding, click 'Create Rule', name the rule 'CCTV-Media', and set External and Internal Port range to 8000.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Rule Name: CCTV-Media... Port 8000 to 8000... Protocol TCP/UDP... Target IP: 192.168.1.150. Added.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Create a second rule named 'CCTV-RTSP' with port 554 pointing to target IP 192.168.1.150.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Rule Name: CCTV-RTSP... Port 554... Target IP 192.168.1.150. Added both rules. Clicking Apply Firewall Rules.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The firewall rules are active. Now we must configure Dynamic DNS so your phone app can connect even when your public IP address changes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Which DDNS provider does the S-Net Hub support?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under Advanced Settings, select Dynamic DNS. Our hub includes free built-in support for No-IP and DynDNS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I already created a free No-IP hostname account yesterday! It is 'watford-connor.ddns.net'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Select No-IP as provider, enter 'watford-connor.ddns.net' in Hostname, along with your No-IP email and password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Entering hostname, email, and password... clicking Update DDNS. Status says 'Connecting to DDNS server...'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The DDNS client has registered your public IP with the authoritative name servers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! The Hub screen refreshed and says 'DDNS Status: Success - Last update today at 11:24 AM'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now disconnect your mobile phone from the home WiFi, switch to 5G cellular mobile data, and launch the CCTV viewing app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Turning off WiFi on my mobile... now on 5G mobile data. Opening the Hik-Connect security camera app.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the server settings of the app, enter 'watford-connor.ddns.net' as the server domain and port 8000.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing watford-connor.ddns.net and port 8000... clicking Connect. The loading wheel is spinning... oh wow!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did the multi-channel video feed load?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All four camera feeds just appeared in real-time high definition! Front driveway, back patio, side gate, and garden! I can see the crystal clear live stream over 5G data!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms external NAT translation and DDNS resolution are fully operational, Connor.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What an enormous relief. Now I can install the app on my wife's phone and she will be able to see every corner of the house wherever she is.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Her phone will connect using the exact same DDNS domain and security credentials.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let us test the pan-tilt-zoom control on the back patio camera to ensure two-way telemetry works.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead, test the PTZ directional controls in the mobile application.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tapping the directional arrow... the camera swiveled smoothly towards the back fence without any delay!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bi-directional TCP handshakes are flowing cleanly across port 8000.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we also test the motion alert notifications to ensure push notifications reach our lock screens?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the app notification settings, enable 'Event Push Notifications' for motion detection zones.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Enabling Event Push Notifications... locking my phone screen now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Walk across the back patio camera line of sight to trigger an intrusion event.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Stepping out onto the patio... my phone immediately buzzed with an alert: 'Motion Detected: Back Patio' with an instant snapshot!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Push notifications traverse the outbound TLS channel without needing additional inbound ports.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives us absolute peace of mind while away from home.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Will these router firewall rules stay saved if the power cuts out or if the router reboots?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I was wondering about that in case of winter power cuts.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The port forwarding rules and DHCP static reservations are written to non-volatile flash memory and persist across power cycles.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is reassuring to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check, Connor, is your home broadband browsing and television streaming performing normally across all your other computers?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our broadband speeds are completely fine, the problem was purely the external camera access.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will remain the dedicated owner for this support case and log the static CCTV port forwarding configuration on your customer file.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Sean, you have brought a massive sense of safety and relief back into our household today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ensure you maintain strong alphanumeric passwords on your camera recorder interface to keep remote access secure.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have created a complex sixteen-character password for the camera system.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your S-Net broadband or router configuration that I can assist you with today, Connor?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that has solved our security camera setup completely. Thank you Sean.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may receive a short customer satisfaction survey by SMS after this call; we would appreciate any feedback you can share.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will fill out the survey. Have a good afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Connor. Stay safe, and take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
